content: Approach and findings. We exploit editor tags and user-generated search terms as input for tag recommendation approaches. Our evaluation comprises of a rich set of 19 different algorithms to recommend tags for e-books, which we group into (i) popularity-based, (ii) similarity-based (i.e., using content information), and (iii) hybrid approaches. We evaluate our approaches in terms of accuracy, semantic similarity and diversity on the review content of Amazon users, which reflects the readers' vocabulary. With semantic similarity, we measure how semantically similar (based on learned Doc2Vec BIBREF7 embeddings) the list of recommended tags is to the list of relevant tags. We use this additional metric to measure not only exact “hits” of our recommendations but also semantic matches.
